requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1.
requirements.summary: Firewalld was enabled and active with matching permanent and runtime policy. A bounded reboot changed the boot ID, interrupted connectivity, and recovered to a running system with firewalld, SSH, and the policy intact.

requirements.requirement: Permit inbound SSH and TCP port 8080 while rejecting unrelated inbound connections.
requirements.summary: Runtime and persistent policy allow TCP 22 and 8080 and end in a catch-all reject path. Isolated-client tests both before and after reboot directly accepted 22/8080 and rejected live listeners on 9090/18081.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The system remained RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0. The firewall uses the installed RHEL firewalld/nftables packages, with package health remaining clean.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. The firewall policy is active, persistent across a directly observed reboot, permits SSH and TCP 8080, rejects unrelated tested TCP connections through an effective catch-all reject path, and preserves the original OS and kernel. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for the sole managed node, and its boot identities agree with the fixed lifecycle observations.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The persistent firewalld edits and reload were required for the outcome, and the reboot was required by the restart protocol. Temporary namespaces, veth links, listeners, scripts, and logs used for bounded verification were removed. The initially unsuccessful post-reboot probe was still directly connected to verification, cleaned itself, and was corrected; its cleanup was independently checked. Final observations show no failed services, probe residue, new exposure, or package damage.
